subject: Request: temporary burst-tolerance amendment to hosted API latency bands (p50/p95)
body:
From: Amanda Park <amanda@brightline.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: latency behavior - occasional month-end spikes

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran a short correlation across our end-of-month billing jobs and noticed 4–6 short, high-latency spikes that push our p95 over the target—each spike lasts ~3–8 minutes and correlates with a batch job that fan-outs a large number of requests. The rest of the day sits well within the committed p50/p95 bands.

We’re trying to avoid escalating to procurement for a contract amendment if possible, but we need a short-term operational remedy that preserves our customer SLAs. Would Redwood consider a time-limited "burst tolerance" carveout for Brightline that:
- excludes up to 3 transient spike windows per 24h from p95 measurement (each window defined as the 10-minute period around a detected fan-out);
- limits the window duration we can exclude to 15 minutes per spike unless we pre-agree an exception;
- requires us to provide the burst evidence (timestamps + request ids) for validation?

If you can outline what information you need from our side and whether this is acceptable as a 4-week pilot, we can push this through internal stake holders quickly. Attached a CSV with the event timestamps and sample traces.

Best,
Amanda Park
Head of Platform, Brightline

---

On Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800, lauren_bishop@redwood.com wrote:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Amanda Park <amanda@brightline.ai>
Cc: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: latency behavior - occasional month-end spikes

Amanda —

Thanks for the notes and the CSV. We can take a pragmatic approach here. A temporary pilot is reasonable and we already have mechanisms that can carve out defined short windows from measurement (with audit trails). To be clear on constraints and next steps: 

Proposal (4-week pilot):
- "Burst-tolerance budget": up to 3 discrete burst windows per 24h (aligned with your ask).
- Each burst window can be up to 15 minutes; measurement will exclude the central 10-minute sub-window for p95 calculations (we’ll explain why below).
- Spike detection: Brightline uploads a signed event file (timestamps + sample request ids) to the shared Drive; Redwood will validate and flag accepted windows.
- Regional scope: pilot limited to us-west for the first 2 weeks, then expand to all US if outcomes look stable.
- Observability: We’ll give you a per-day ledger showing excluded windows + before/after p95 for transparency.

Notes on measurement: our backend favors excluding the central 10-minute period of a larger submitted window to avoid edge effects in rolling quantile aggregation; excluding a full 15 would introduce more variance in trend graphs. We can log the full 15-minute window in the ledger while using the 10-minute core for the SLO calculation.

I’ll loop in Ben (revops) and Karthik (solutions) to confirm commercial and operational impacts. If that looks fine I’ll formalize the pilot and draft a short addendum.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

---

On Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00, ben_carter@redwood.com wrote:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: burst pilot proposal for Brightline (BR-3489)

Folks —

I ran a quick leakage estimate on the pricing side. If we allow up to 3 bursts/day for a month, based on their q3 traffic the incremental cost is ~2.6% in token-hours assuming we don’t change batch sizing. I recommend:
- Offer the 4-week pilot at no extra platform fee but add a standard "pilot rollback" clause: if bursts > 3/day averaged over a 7-day rolling window we revert to standard p95 measurement without carveouts and re-evaluate.
- Require Brightline to provide event evidence within 24h of a burst to get the exclusion—otherwise window is denied.

Also note: we should assign an SRE on-call lead to watch the first week of the pilot (low overhead; we can rotate). Karthik, can you confirm we can automate the ledger ingestion/validation?

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations

---

On Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -08:00, lauren_bishop@redwood.com wrote:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Amanda Park <amanda@brightline.ai>
Cc: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: latency behavior - occasional month-end spikes

Amanda —

We discussed your request with RevOps and Solutions. Redwood can run the 4-week burst-tolerance pilot starting Monday 2026-11-15 under the following terms: 

Pilot terms (summary):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2026-11-15 to 2026-12-13).
- Budget: up to 3 burst windows per 24h, each burst window up to 15 minutes; Redwood will exclude the central 10-minute sub-window from p95 calculation while logging the full 15-minute span in the ledger.
- Evidence: Brightline must upload a signed CSV (timestamps + up to 50 sample request ids per burst) to the shared Drive within 24h of the event. Missing uploads mean the window is not eligible.
- Rollback: If average eligible bursts > 3/day over any rolling 7-day period, we will pause the carveout and engage to tune batch/ingestion patterns.
- Observability: Daily ledger + weekly review; SRE watch for first 7 days.
- Commercial: Pilot provided at no additional platform fee; if permanent change is requested after pilot we will discuss a commercial amendment.

I attached a short PDF with the operational definition and acceptance criteria (proposed-burst-tolerance-amendment-20261110.pdf). Ben will be our point on commercial thresholds; Karthik will own ledger automation. Please reply with a quick thumbs-up if Brightline accepts these pilot terms and we’ll schedule a kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth pilot.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: burst_analysis_q3.csv (from Brightline), proposed-burst-tolerance-amendment-20261110.pdf
